question: Is the narrow Azure SAP HANA Intel-retention example currently accurate, and does a verified current Xeon 6 buyer deployment establish the margin mechanism?

verdict.main_page_5_narrow_claim: Supported by current Microsoft FAQ and independently checked live SAP certification-directory filters. No mandatory wording change.
verdict.forecast_change: None. Certification supports switching-friction reasoning, not a numerical net-price, market-share or profit-margin floor.
verdict.new_generation_buyer_proof: Not established in this targeted check. The strongest named buyer case discovered has an internally conflicting Xeon 6 headline and older-generation deployed systems in its body.

sap_directory_live_observation.observation_window_utc: 2026-11-05 23:52 to 23:57 UTC; precise first UI timestamp not separately measured
sap_directory_live_observation.method: Browser visible DOM/accessibility only. Selected Certified IaaS Platforms and Microsoft Azure; active tag Certified Solutions; opened CPU Architecture filter. No hidden application state or network API used.
scope_limits: 237 are certification records, not customers, sold units, independent workloads, or revenue shares. Some VM names repeat.
This filter establishes currently listed certified Azure IaaS platforms, not every SAP product, managed service or future certification.
SAP directory certification is successful integration; certification does not guarantee error-free vendor operation.
Absence of Granite Rapids in the selected directory plus preview documentation does not prove no pilot or private trial exists.
sap_directory_live_observation.receipt: Observed UI content transcribed into this structured receipt and present in tool transcript. Export-as-PDF attempt timed out; no exported PDF was captured. Research tab closed after inspection.

primary_document_checks.locator: You want to know; question on Da(s)v4/Ea(s) not certified for SAP HANA
primary_document_checks.fact: Microsoft still attributes lack of SAP HANA certification on these Azure families to AMD CPU hardware.
primary_document_checks.boundary: The pitch uses a narrower Azure VM statement and separately discloses managed HANA Cloud Arm support.

primary_document_checks.locator: SAP HANA supported Azure virtual machines
primary_document_checks.fact: Microsoft designates the SAP HANA hardware directory as the source of truth; NetWeaver certification is not sufficient for HANA.

primary_document_checks.locator: Title, Host specifications and last-updated footer
primary_document_checks.fact: Msv4 Medium Memory is explicitly Preview, based on Granite Rapids/Xeon 6; updated 2026-09-15.
Mdsv4 Medium Memory is also explicitly Preview and based on Granite Rapids/Xeon 6.
VMware describes Xeon 6 P-core two-socket support for HANA on vSAN/VCF 9.1.
primary_document_checks.boundary: Software support establishes an available migration path; it is not an enterprise buyer deployment, independent ROI or measured Intel profit.

primary_document_checks.fact: HPE announces available Xeon 6 Scale-up Server 3250 and a large-memory HANA benchmark.
primary_document_checks.boundary: No named actual enterprise buyer outcome found in the release; vendor product/benchmark evidence only. Read by web tool; archival direct download timed out.

toyota_case_generation_conflict.publication_date: Not clearly stated in page reviewed; do not invent a publication date.
toyota_case_generation_conflict.headline_claim: Headline and overview refer to Xeon 6.
body_locators: Solution | Supporting workloads using Amazon EC2 U7i and R6i instances
Outcome | Rolling out a new architecture for SAP in under two weeks
toyota_case_generation_conflict.body_facts: Toyota migrated SAP to U7i with R6i; AWS reports financial closing improved from 72 hours to under 24 hours, with 1.5-times engineering performance. The same body describes R8i/R8i-flex and X8i Xeon 6 instances as being evaluated for the future.

matched_specs.fact: U7i uses 4th Generation Xeon Sapphire Rapids; the page also carries a Toyota U7i migration testimonial.
R6i uses 3rd Generation Xeon Ice Lake.

toyota_case_generation_conflict.adjudication: Reject attribution of these realized gains to Xeon 6. Preserve only as supplier-hosted reported Intel-to-Intel modernization and migration outcome, with explicitly unresolved title/body inconsistency.
toyota_case_generation_conflict.source_independence: Named Toyota manager quotes on AWS marketing pages; not a Toyota-authored engineering report or independent experiment.
economic_limits: No comparable AMD/Arm alternative evaluation, purchase invoice, contractual CPU price, Intel realized ASP or margin.
Architecture changed compute, memory and operational process together; no CPU-generation causal isolation.
An advertised up-to 45% U7i price/performance claim is an AWS product-level statement, not Toyota actual savings or Intel economics.
toyota_case_generation_conflict.rejected_search_host: Search initially surfaced a non-AWS lookalike hostname. It was not used as evidence; the official aws.amazon.com page was opened directly and archived.

search_rejection_log.candidate: Intel IT commercial database licensing case
search_rejection_log.reason: Prior review already showed implemented older generation; proposed Xeon 6 improvement is counterfactual, and Intel is the reporting vendor.

search_rejection_log.candidate: Intel/SAP partner testimonial and HPE/Dell/Lenovo validation designs
search_rejection_log.reason: Vendor/partner support or lab benchmarks; not independently reported enterprise deployment economics.
Explicitly commissioned by Intel; not actual independent enterprise workload economics.

search_rejection_log.candidate: ClickHouse hardware benchmark and Phoronix software testing
search_rejection_log.reason: Benchmarks are relevant to technical options but do not answer this buyer-deployment question; no added quantitative forecast inference.

recommended_use: Keep narrow Azure certification example and managed-HANA-Cloud boundary. Do not add the Toyota headline as Xeon 6 proof or use directory counts to calculate share. The unresolved retained-profit evidence remains customer-level Intel net-price/mix and cost retention after supply normalizes.
